drivers.driver: The earnings yield on equities is significantly below the yield on risk-free government bonds, making stocks unattractive relative to alternatives [D04].
Aggregate market valuations, at nearly 29 times trailing earnings, leave little margin of safety for the investor [D04].
Investor sentiment is exuberant, with newer market participants expecting unsustainable annual returns of 22.6% [D03].
Berkshire's discipline requires buying only wonderful businesses at fair prices, a condition not met by current market levels [D08].

final.memo:
Charlie and I find that the current environment offers little in the way of sensible investment opportunities. When the earnings yield of the market is trailing the yield on a 10-year government bond by over 2.5 percentage points, Mr. Market is clearly pricing in an optimism that we simply cannot share [D04]. We have seen this movie before; when valuations become untethered from the underlying economics of the businesses, the only prudent course is to maintain our cash position and wait for a more rational period [D01, D08].

We are not in the business of forecasting the next shift in the market, but we are in the business of demanding a margin of safety [D01]. Today, that safety is nowhere to be found among broad market indices or the popular tech-heavy valuations that seem to dominate the conversation [D04, D06]. We will continue to hold our wonderful businesses—those with durable moats and capable managers—but we will not be adding to our positions at these prices [D08]. Patience is not just a virtue in this business; it is a necessity for the preservation of capital.
